findings.F1: The short side does not pay for itself: summed bar gains of short positions were -0.004 in falling 30-day markets and -0.19 in rising ones, against fees of -0.23 and -0.16; long positions earned +1.27 and +2.52 against fees of -0.28 and -0.21; narrower-than-norm cases had a 3-day excess of only -0.16 % (t -1.16, n 3570), while wider cases had +0.26 % (t 1.40, n 2153).
findings.F2: The effect lives only while the coin's 30-day return is positive: there the pooled slope of 3-day excess on the forecast is 0.00284 (t 3.96, n 2187), and when it is negative it is -0.00047 (t -0.63, n 2096); the 3-day excess rises in steps in rising markets (-0.27 %, -0.05 %, -0.27 %, +0.56 %, +2.03 % with t 3.71 at the widest, n 345).
findings.F3: A rising 30-day return is not an effect of its own: in rising markets, grid cases without a wide day had 3-day excess of -0.19 % (n 1585), against +1.40 % (t 3.79, n 602) when the day was also wider than its norm; in falling markets wide days gave -0.31 % (n 670). The trend belongs to the idea's own theory, because range expansion that follows a trend is trend-following traders adding, not panic.
findings.F4: The book's deepest falls came in falling windows: w9 fell -12.9 % while its coins fell 32 %, and w2 fell -9.2 % while its coins fell 44 %, with long positions losing -0.25 in w2. Being long on wide days inside a downtrend is what feeds the Calmar failure (0.42).
findings.F5: The book was in a position on 99 % of coin-days, mostly with small positions near a zero forecast (mean |allocation| 0.09–0.11 for |f| < 1.5, 14 % of bars with |f| < 0.5). That is why the mean on days in a position is 0.016 % against the required 0.05 %, while the bars with f > 3 carried +2.34 of the +3.6 summed gain.
findings.F6: The move is large against the cost where the effect holds: wide days in rising markets were followed by a total 3-day move of +1.77 % (9 times the 0.19 % trade cost) and a 6-day move of +3.28 % (excess +2.54 %, t 2.93, n 310), while the 10-day move fades (t 1.46).
findings.F7: Wide days that close down carry the effect too (3-day excess +0.88 %, t 2.47, n 612), against +0.15 % (t 0.42) on wide days that close up. Unlike the trend, this is a split inside the signal, not a separate condition.

ideas.idea: The further a coin's daily high-low range exceeds its average range over the past 30 days, the higher that coin's return over the next 3 days above its usual drift, only while the coin's 30-day return is positive.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long after unusually wide days in coins that are up over the past month, more strongly the wider the day, and stay out of the market otherwise, which cuts both the downtrend falls and the idle low-forecast days.
ideas.name: wide days in uptrends rise

ideas.idea: The further a coin's daily high-low range exceeds its average range over the past 30 days, the higher that coin's return over the next 3 days above its usual drift, with no lean against the coin after narrower days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would take only the long side after wide days, sized with the width, and drop the short side, which earns nothing and pays fees.
ideas.name: range expansion long side only

ideas.idea: The further a coin's daily high-low range exceeds its average range over the past 30 days, the higher that coin's return over the next 6 days above its usual drift, while the coin's 30-day return is positive.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold the long after a wide day in an uptrend for about a week, catching a larger move per trade against the same cost.
ideas.name: wide uptrend days held longer
